content:
Farrand Hall is a historic dormitory building located on the University of Colorado Boulder campus. It was named after Frederick Allen Farrand, a former professor of history and principal of the university from 1888 to 1903. The building was completed in 1910 and is one of the oldest buildings on campus.

Farrand Hall has a traditional collegiate Gothic architectural style, featuring red brick walls, tall windows, and a central tower. It originally housed only male students, but later became co-ed.

The building offers dormitory-style housing for undergraduate students, with shared bathroom facilities and common areas. It is known for its communal atmosphere and social events, making it a popular choice among students.

Farrand Hall is located near many academic buildings and campus amenities, making it a convenient housing option for students. It is also close to the University Memorial Center, which houses dining facilities, study spaces, and student services.

Overall, Farrand Hall is a beloved and historic building on the University of Colorado Boulder campus, offering a unique living experience for students.
